criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: The introduction thoroughly answers all requirements: the mission rationale and primary purpose (monitoring Great Barrier Reef coral bleaching using fluid lensing), the rationale for a single spacecraft, and the operators/users (Australian science agencies/government). Referencing is well integrated.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report structure is readable with good sectioning. However, presentation has flaws: figures and tables lack formal figure/table numbers and standardized captions (e.g., Image 1 has text underneath without numbering, Image 3 has no caption). A sentence is truncated mid-clause in the EOL section, and Wikipedia is cited as source [6] despite explicit instructions forbidding it.

overall: A solid, well-conceived mission design focused on Australian reef conservation with appropriate orbital analysis and STK access simulation. Improvements are needed in formal figure/table numbering and captions, proofreading unfinished text, avoiding Wikipedia as a source, and ensuring raw simulation files are included.

feedback.summary: You have produced a well-conceived, technically sound mission design for Australian coral bleaching monitoring using STK analysis and clear engineering rationale. Your mission concept, orbital elements, and ground access analyses were particularly well developed. To reach the top grade band, you need to refine your professional presentation by establishing standard captioning, proofreading for incomplete sentences, replacing informal sources with peer-reviewed literature, and attaching the required simulation data files.
next_steps: Apply standard engineering captioning across all visual elements by formally numbering and labeling every figure and table (e.g., Image 1, Image 3) consistently throughout the document.
Perform a thorough final proofread of all narrative sections, ensuring incomplete sentences such as the drag sail explanation in 'Mission Duration & EOL' are corrected.
Replace unauthorized references like Wikipedia (citation [6]) with academic literature or official launch provider manuals, and attach all raw STK/simulation files alongside your report.

criteria.C1: You articulated an excellent mission rationale in the Introduction, justifying single-satellite fluid lensing for coral bleaching and defining clear stakeholders like CSIRO. To maintain this top standard, continue backing operational needs with specific mission requirements.
criteria.C2: Your orbital mechanics, Vega E launch selection, and ground station access intervals in STK were well developed. To reach the highest tier, complete all truncated explanations (such as the drag sail mechanics) and submit the raw software data files.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion effectively synthesized the engineering findings and trade-offs into a coherent summary. To achieve full marks, tie your final conclusions directly to quantified mission performance metrics derived from your analysis.
criteria.C4: Your sectioning is clear, but presentation fell to Adequate due to unnumbered/missing figure captions, an unfinished sentence in the EOL section, and citing Wikipedia ([6]). To reach Accomplished, implement formal captioning, eliminate non-academic sources, and proofread carefully.
